recovery.title: 1. Recovery (bouncing back)
recovery.growth: The economy has passed its lowest point and starts growing again, though activity is still below its normal long-term level.
recovery.jobs: Layoffs slow down. Companies first ask existing staff to work overtime before opening large new hiring drives.
recovery.prices: Inflation stays calm and comfortable because factories and workers still have plenty of spare capacity.
recovery.borrowing: Interest rates are usually low to encourage families and businesses to borrow and spend again.
recovery.everyday: Stores offer good deals, EMIs feel lighter, and stock markets often start rising months before daily news feels cheerful.

expansion.title: 2. Expansion / boom (India today)
expansion.growth: Business activity climbs above its long-term normal trend. Factories run near full speed and companies build new plants.
expansion.jobs: Hiring is strong across sectors and unemployment drops. Late in a boom, skilled workers become harder to find.
expansion.prices: Prices start rising faster as strong demand meets limited supply, pushing inflation above central bank comfort zones.
expansion.borrowing: Loan demand surges for homes, cars, and business expansion. Central banks begin nudging interest rates up to prevent overheating.
expansion.everyday: Showrooms and malls are packed, salaries and stock portfolios look healthy, but grocery bills and new loan EMIs start creeping higher.

slowdown.title: 3. Slowdown (easing off the gas)
slowdown.growth: The economy is still growing above normal, but the speed starts slowing down after passing its peak.
slowdown.jobs: Companies keep hiring, but much more selectively and at a slower pace than during the boom.
slowdown.prices: Inflation stays stubborn near the peak before slowly cooling off after higher interest rates bite.
slowdown.borrowing: Higher interest rates make home, car, and business loans costlier, so credit growth gradually moderates.
slowdown.everyday: Sales slow slightly before factories cut output, so unsold stock builds up. Investors begin preferring steady, defensive businesses.

contraction.title: 4. Contraction (downturn)
contraction.growth: Economic activity drops below its normal trend. If the drop is broad and lasts long enough, it becomes a recession.
contraction.jobs: Companies first cut overtime and freeze new hiring, and may later trim staff if sales stay weak. Unemployment rises.
contraction.prices: Price rises slow down noticeably (disinflation) as families hold back on non-essential spending.
contraction.borrowing: Banks get cautious about lending, while the central bank cuts interest rates to support the economy.
contraction.everyday: Families delay big purchases like cars or holidays, focus on essentials, and favor safer savings like government bonds and fixed deposits.
